text: The five consumed rows are class C contract dependencies even though the plan's C row is empty; the approval slice binds to the published documents and their fakes on Day 1 and the real services arrive in integration.
why: R5.4 says a C dependency never blocks the build and R5.7 rule 2 says an APP story builds against CON stories and their fakes, so an empty C row changes the dependency map only.
read: R5.4; R5.7; plan slices RWB-S6-E6001-APP and RWB-S6-E6001-CON; TSD S6 T5.2
impact: None on Day 1; the integration order of the wave 4 harness only.

text: The approval chain, the approver's act, the ledger entry and the DoA limit stay with rwb-decision and rwb-access; rwb-debtsale starts the child approval, reads the answer and writes no approval row.
why: The kit's Approval template is named for the DoA approvals of S2, S3, S5, S6 and S7, and the service owns no approval table in its ownership rows.
read: Context pack Temporal slide 12; context pack ownership rows; TSD S6 T5.2
impact: The service keeps one table pair and no approval schema; a later change of owner is a contract change, not a rebuild.

text: Where no source publishes an operation name, the contract uses the section R9 placeholder and a fake, and the row is re-tagged when the owner publishes the name.
why: The names of the approval act form, the rule-package read and the case-move answer are not published and R9 forbids inventing a value.
read: R9; TSD S6 T5.2; Architecture v5 slide 14
impact: A placeholder name in the contract and in the fakes, replaced without a change of behaviour.

text: The service owns one event, EV-23 LotAwarded, and it is published by the award story; this legacy key declares no event of its own and its approval leaves on the case-move answer and the read.
why: The ownership rows give one event and the TSD gives LotAwarded as the published event; the legacy story lists no event and no source names an approval event.
read: Context pack ownership rows; TSD S6 T5.3
impact: No producer in the approval step; a consumer of the approval reads the case state or the lot read.

text: The Credit approval committee member of the FSD is read as an approval-chain answer under the rwb-access DoA limit, not as a Workbench role; the T6.1 rights apply to the read unchanged.
why: The TSD RBAC matrix has no committee row and no source publishes a delegation-limit row for it, so the act cannot be expressed as a Workbench right.
read: FSD S6 A2.5.3.3; TSD S6 T6.1
impact: The authority written on the lot comes from the approval answer; no new role or grant is created.
